title: The Cloud Connection
question: Which cloud identity and workload boundary can explain an application action that endpoint records cannot cover?
briefing: An application integration performed a cloud storage operation. The available workstation record is quiet, but it cannot observe actions performed by the cloud workload identity. Your authority is to acquire records and recommend a session-scoped response through Cloud Identity Operations. You cannot approve your own control or disable an entire account or service.
lesson: A workload identity belongs to an application or service; it is distinct from a person’s endpoint session.

entities.name: Cloud workload identity session
entities.impact: The integration delivers customer-service documents. Restricting the named workload session does not stop every app or remove all storage permissions.
entities.capability: Named session and disclosed source paths only; no account-wide or host-wide control.
entities.dependency: The integration delivers customer-service documents. Restricting the named workload session does not stop every app or remove all storage permissions.

entities.name: APP-08 context
entities.purpose: Related context that must be assessed separately
entities.impact: Do not generalise the primary session finding to this separate scope.
entities.capability: Only the explicitly delivered relationship and source records.
entities.dependency: A separate task or observation does not supply approval for the primary session.

options.label: Treat a quiet workstation source as coverage of all cloud actions
Pivot from the app to the acquired workload identity and cloud audit
Claim that one app session covers every cloud identity

limits.label: Workstation collection cannot establish the absence of actions executed by a delegated cloud workload.
Unavailable collection does not establish that no activity occurred.
The source identifies a session or credential, not a person or motive.
Other scopes and their remaining questions need their own evidence.

queries.label: Establish the task and business consequence
queries.question: What is this service for, and which consequences change investigation priority?
queries.can: Names the normal task, related scopes, owners and interruption consequence.
queries.cannot: Does not establish who performed the current action.

queries.label: Check the exact work authorisation
queries.question: Does approved work cover this session, task, target and period?
queries.cannot: Does not prove the human operator or the activity that actually occurred.

queries.label: Inspect the scoped session activity
queries.question: Which action was recorded for this named session within collection limits?
queries.can: Records session-level actions and the observed target.
queries.cannot: Cannot identify a person, establish motive or reconstruct missing historical collection.

queries.label: Check the service transaction independently
queries.question: Does the service-side transaction establish the same scoped operation?
queries.can: Tests the operation through a separately collected service transaction.
queries.cannot: A second card alone does not establish a sufficient explanation.

queries.label: Read the enabled future observation window
queries.question: Did the explicitly generated harmless event reach collection after activation?
queries.can: Tests this named source capability, target and future event time only.
queries.cannot: Cannot backfill any missing historical interval or prove broader coverage.

facts.title: Starting observations
facts.text: An application integration performed a cloud storage operation. The available workstation record is quiet, but it cannot observe actions performed by the cloud workload identity.

facts.title: Task, scope and business consequence
facts.text: APP-08 delegates a limited document-synchronisation job to WORKLOAD-S8. Endpoint process records cover the workstation; cloud identity and object audits cover the delegated storage action.

facts.title: The specific work authorisation
facts.text: The integration change record approves the workload session, document collection and read-only object operation within this review period.

facts.title: Recorded session activity
facts.text: The workload session read the document collection named in the integration record. This cloud operation is not expected to appear as a workstation process.

facts.title: An independently collected transaction
facts.text: The storage object audit independently records the approved document read by the delegated workload session.

facts.title: Verified business-context response
facts.text: A pre-established directory contact confirmed the task record: The integration change record approves the workload session, document collection and read-only object operation within this review period. This confirms the business record, not the person operating the session.

facts.title: The specific work authorisation
facts.text: The integration change record approves read-only document synchronisation. It contains no approval for changing the storage access policy through this workload session.

facts.title: Recorded session activity
facts.text: The workload session submitted a storage-access-policy change outside its read-only integration task. The endpoint’s quiet result cannot contradict this cloud audit.

facts.title: An independently collected transaction
facts.text: The storage policy audit independently records the policy-change request tied to the delegated workload session and the affected document collection.

facts.title: Verified business-context response
facts.text: A pre-established directory contact confirmed the task record: The integration change record approves read-only document synchronisation. It contains no approval for changing the storage access policy through this workload session. This confirms the business record, not the person operating the session.

facts.title: Work record unavailable
facts.text: The work-authorisation archive is unavailable for the named session and period. No approval or denial can be inferred.

facts.title: Session collection unavailable
facts.text: The session-audit source did not collect the relevant historical interval. Absence of a record cannot establish the absence of activity.

facts.title: Independent collection is limited
facts.text: The independent service journal lacks the target application operation for the historical interval. A different source name does not restore that capability.

facts.title: Verified check timed out
facts.text: The pre-established directory contact did not respond by the stated due step. This is a delivered limitation, not approval or a reason to wait indefinitely.

facts.title: Future-only source verification
facts.text: A harmless verification event was collected after the enabled source window began. It establishes collection only for this target, capability and time; it cannot restore historical coverage.
caveats: A successful test now does not establish historical coverage.

response.control: Restrict only the named organisation-controlled session

glossary.definition: A workload identity belongs to an application or service; it is distinct from a person’s endpoint session.
The target, operation and interval a source is capable of observing.

reviewWindow: The named session from its start through the explicit cutoff of each acquired snapshot. A simulation step is an investigation opportunity, not a minute.
